claim_being_audited: That certification may proceed for this model only as a disclosed certification: aggregate readiness is supported, the small-business support slice shows an unresolved weakness, no approved mitigation exists, and clean certification without explicit disclosure is not evidentially supported.
specific_concerns: The packet is directionally well supported, but it does not establish with admissible evidence whether the small-business support slice is definitively a material weakness or a protected/contractual segment under the disclosure rule.
The actor moves from threshold underperformance to a firm disclosure obligation without a separate admissible materiality determination.
Small-sample uncertainty is correctly not treated as exculpatory, but it does leave the magnitude and stability of the slice weakness less certain than the packet implies.
unsupported_claims: The categorical claim that certification must carry explicit disclosure is not fully proved unless the record also establishes the slice weakness as material under policy.
The claim that minor-caveat wording is definitively insufficient is not fully supported without admissible evidence on materiality classification or required model-card wording.
evidence_requests: Provide the admissible record showing whether the small-business support slice is a protected or contractual customer segment, or otherwise why it is classified as materially affected under policy.
Provide any admissible materiality assessment, escalation note, or model-card review guidance that maps this slice result to mandatory disclosure language.
Provide the exact approved certification/disclosure template or required wording standard, if one exists.
decision_criteria: Aggregate performance support exists only for launch readiness, not for erasing subgroup weaknesses.
Certification is compliant only if any material weakness is disclosed or an approved mitigation removes exposure.
An unapproved draft mitigation cannot be treated as satisfying the mitigation exception.
Small-sample uncertainty can justify follow-up confirmation, but not clean certification when the materiality predicate remains unresolved.
A fully compliant verdict would require admissible evidence tying this slice weakness to the policy's materiality/disclosure trigger.
